# Extract from documents: PostgreSQL

**Pattern:** File Processing · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers ocr-&-extraction work end to end across PostgreSQL, Google Drive and Slack.

It moves through 20 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. List Changed Docs (Google Drive)
3. Remove Duplicate Documents
4. Download File Content
5. Extract Text from File
6. Attach Chunk Metadata
7. Insert into Vector Store
8. Prepare Documents
9. Chunk with Overlap
10. Document Embeddings
11. Count Indexed Chunks
12. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
13. Archive Copy to Google Drive
14. Load Previous Snapshot
15. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
16. Fingerprint for Idempotency
17. Drop Already-Processed Items
18. Summarize Run Stats
19. Append Audit Row (PostgreSQL)
20. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing ocr-&-extraction work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → List Changed Docs (Google Drive) → Remove Duplicate Documents → Download File Content → Extract Text from File → Attach Chunk Metadata → Insert into Vector Store → Prepare Documents → Chunk with Overlap → Document Embeddings → Count Indexed Chunks → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Copy to Google Drive → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (PostgreSQL) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping PostgreSQL and Google Drive aligned by hand for ocr & extraction
- Answering ocr-&-extraction questions from your own indexed documents, then replying in PostgreSQL
- Ocr & extraction work where "List Changed Docs (Google Drive)" is still a manual step before PostgreSQL
- Ocr & extraction work that only reaches PostgreSQL on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps PostgreSQL and Google Drive in step for ocr & extraction, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in PostgreSQL or Google Drive are skipped, across all 23 nodes of this ocr-&-extraction build
- A failed PostgreSQL or Google Drive call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 23 nodes in this ocr-&-extraction build
- Fans the same result out to Slack in the same run, for ocr & extraction
- Ocr-&-extraction answers come from your indexed content, not model recall, before reaching PostgreSQL

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2; OpenAI API key; Postgres connection; Qdrant URL + key; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Ingestion is a separate workflow from querying because indexing and answering have different triggers, schedules, and failure modes — a slow re-index should never block a live user question. Chunking with overlap (not whole documents) keeps each retrieval hit focused on relevant text instead of dragging in an entire document's unrelated sections.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Change chunkSize and chunkOverlap, then compare retrieval quality back in the query workflow.
2. Add a second file source and normalize both into the same chunk-metadata shape.
3. Swap the embedding model — but change it in both this workflow and the query workflow, since they must match.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Service Accounts have their own empty Drive — share the target folder with it.

**Qdrant URL + key**
Qdrant Cloud → cluster URL + API key (or your self-hosted URL).
_Gotcha:_ Create the collection with the right vector size before inserting.

**OpenAI API key**
Same OpenAI API key as the chat model.
_Gotcha:_ Indexing and querying MUST use the same embedding model or retrieval breaks.

**Postgres connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your Postgres provider.
_Gotcha:_ Managed providers usually require SSL enabled in the credential's options.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Retrieval returns nothing or irrelevant chunks**
Cause: Index is empty, or indexing and querying used different embedding models.
Fix: Run the ingestion workflow first, and make sure both sides use the identical embedding model.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your ocr & extraction process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- PostgreSQL: connect as a role that can reach only the tables below, not as the owner.
- Google Drive: scope the credential to the one folder this workflow writes to, not `drive.readonly` across the account.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole ocr-&-extraction payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
